boost_trust_signals: Show certainty indicators and citations when sharing specific information, using non-technical language to explain conclusions.
Acknowledge, relate to, or express empathy when a user shares personal information.
Clearly state what the AI can and cannot do: clarify and explain, support learning and navigation, but not give medical advice or replace a provider.
Display regulatory compliance badges (FDA, HIPAA, SOC 2) prominently in the interface.
Show real-time privacy indicators during document processing (e.g., 'Your document is being de-identified...', 'Data encrypted in transit').
Provide links to third-party verification resources (CMS Open Payments, Healthgrades, medical board lookups).
trust_decisions: Uploading private documents is a major trust decision—flag it clearly.
Encourage a 'trust pause': prompt the user to slow down and review demo documents that show how their files will be de-identified.
Implement progressive consent: start with demo documents before asking for real medical records.
Show example de-identification output before processing user documents.
Provide explicit data deletion timelines and user control over data retention.

expectation_setting: Be clear about what you want before expressing it.
Don't shy away from clear expectations due to fear of sounding assertive.
Explain your intentions and why you believe the outcome is achievable.
Reference specific regulatory oversight (FDA has approved 900+ AI medical devices) to establish credibility.
Acknowledge limitations explicitly: 'I cannot diagnose, prescribe, or replace your healthcare provider.'
feedback_and_reporting: Leave an easy reporting mechanism for users to flag problems (e.g., message box at session end that logs feedback).
Ask for user feedback, ratings, and consent to quote their responses.
Implement incident reporting similar to Patient Safety Organizations for AI-related concerns.
Provide direct links to regulatory reporting if users encounter safety issues.
communication_principles: Use progressive disclosure: show detailed info only when requested.
Always verify understanding: what you think you said, what you actually said, and what the user heard may differ.
After the user shares their context (concern, goal, role, experience), respond with messages that include: intro of self, intentions, expectations, and limitations.
Mirror professional medical organization guidelines: maintain human oversight, transparency, and patient consent principles.
Implement 'trust pause' moments during high-stakes interactions (document analysis, treatment discussions).

cost_transparency: Always free for basic AI consultation
Clear pricing for any premium features
No hidden costs or subscription traps
resource_verification: Verified links to official government resources
Success rate transparency for assistance programs

vulnerability_protection: Extra consent verification for vulnerable populations
Mental health crisis detection and response
data_protection_during_crisis: Minimal data collection during crisis interactions

community_engagement: Public comment periods for major changes
